selection_policy: Distance first using nominal heliocentric distances. Supported regular spheroids only; confirmed-real and confirmed-galaxy flags required; exclude clusters, existing aliases, insufficient geometry and reviewed disputed/disrupting systems. Gaussian extent is an estimate based on measured half-light size. No artificial spiral morphology.

draco_2.reason: Current literature still debates galaxy versus star-cluster status; defer this object.

carina_3.reason: Sparse spectroscopy leaves a conservative galaxy/cluster classification; defer this object.

willman_1.reason: Current spectroscopy still describes the galaxy/cluster classification as ambiguous.

sagittarius_1.reason: Actively disrupting, extremely extended system; the current bounded smooth templates do not represent its full structure.

uncertainty_notes.triangulum_2: Binary-star effects leave the internal velocity dispersion and dark-matter content uncertain.
uncertainty_notes.bootes_3: Tidal-remnant structure is possible; only a smooth central component is represented.
uncertainty_notes.ursa_major_2: Possible tidal structure is not reconstructed.
uncertainty_notes.grus_2: Internal velocity dispersion is unresolved; the mass is a stellar-light proxy.
uncertainty_notes.antlia_2: Very diffuse and potentially tidally stripped; only a smooth component is approximated.
uncertainty_notes.delve_2: Galaxy classification follows the recent catalog update; the sparse stellar sample adds uncertainty.
